questions.question: 0-0.5s SETUP: does this happen on screen - HOLLIS looks at ELI?
0.5-4.7s ACTION: does this happen on screen - HOLLIS speaks to ELI curtly?
4.7-6s HOLD: does this happen on screen - HOLLIS holds ELI's look, quite still?
Happens exactly once (not repeated or looped): HOLLIS speaks to ELI
HOLLIS: does the face/body read as guarded, impatient (restrained)? Must NOT read as: friendliness.
Line 91 is audible, spoken by the right character, lips match: HOLLIS: Nobody asked you, Moreno. Stand where you're standing and stay quiet.
HOLLIS sounds like the voice bible: low, gravelly male voice; no reference take yet (the first accepted speaking take becomes it)
Planned size CLOSE, EYE_LEVEL, STATIC: does the take match?

First frame matches state SC01_g15: Continues from the previous shot: HOLLIS standing behind the counter; NAOMI standing at the counter, frame-left; ELI standing by the door, frame-right; the brown packet: lying sealed on the counter, red seal up; the ledger: lying open on the counter, pages facing HOLLIS, away from the camera.

Last frame matches state SC01_g16: Continues from the previous shot: HOLLIS standing behind the counter; NAOMI standing at the counter, frame-left; ELI standing by the door, frame-right; the brown packet: lying sealed on the counter, red seal up; the ledger: lying open on the counter, pages facing HOLLIS, away from the camera.
Identity, wardrobe, set and light stable; no morphing, extra limbs, text artefacts or flicker.
Motion is physically plausible and smooth (full clip, not stills).
Line 91: does HOLLIS clearly speak to ELI (eyes and body toward them)?
Is the place where ELI stands kept out of frame (never shown empty), and do HOLLIS's eyes go just past the lens to frame-right?
Does HOLLIS look at ELI and never into the lens?
Do ELI and HOLLIS stay on their own sides (frosted-glass hallway door / counter, staff side and archive shelves) the whole clip?

instructions: Fill checks[] (result, severity on FAIL, level, evidence, reviewer human:<id>), then `film.py review --film DIR --ingest FILE`. Leave a group UNASSESSED if you did not look.
